newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING UNITS LIFT BASE LENDING RATE.
newsitem.headline: ING UNITS LIFT BASE LENDING RATE.

text.p: ING Groep units ING Bank and Postbank will raise their base lending rate to 3.25 percent from 3.00 percent from Monday, ING Bank said on Friday.
"The base lending rate is being raised because of developments in the money market," ING Bank said.
This rate is the basis for setting interest rates on overdrafts of business clients, with each client paying a premium above the base rate.
The Dutch central bank has raised interest rates twice in the last two weeks in a bid to stabilise the guilder, which had been falling against the mark.
Last Monday, it increased the secured loans rate to 2.50 percent from 2.00 percent and the special advances rate to 2.90 percent from 2.70 percent.
It had raised the special advances rate, which sets the tone for money market rates, on February 27 to 2.70 percent from 2.50 percent.
The secured loans rate sets the floor for money market rates.
